hook.text: In 1984, Kamoya Kimeu spotted a skull fragment near Lake Turkana, Kenya. It led to an astonishing find.

buildup.text: The nearly complete skeleton of a boy who died 1.5 million years ago—Homo erectus, roughly age 8–11.

discovery.text: Turkana Boy stood 1.6 metres tall and would have reached 1.85 metres as an adult—modern human height.

twist.text: His body was built for distance walking in heat: long legs, narrow hips, barrel chest. Like a marathon runner.

climax.text: He's the most complete early human skeleton ever found—a single individual who tells a species' story.

punchline.text: One boy's bones mapped a million-year stride.
